content.text:
Now I have the requirements and prior data. Let me analyze the key patterns.

**Key observations from the prior constellation:**
- R1-screen follows a clean linear model: T ≈ 399 + 60·Σ(tᵢ/kᵢ), where t is thickness (mm) and k is conductivity (W/mK). This is never binding for thin plates (limit 420K allows huge thicknesses).
- R2-hotspot (the real FE constraint, ≤340K) is strikingly **flat with thickness** for a given material: aluminium reads 324K at 10/20/30mm, graphite reads 325K at 10/20/30mm, copper reads 322K at 10/20/30mm. This suggests spreading resistance is already saturated by 10mm — the plate is well past the thickness where further material helps, and hotspot is dominated by something largely thickness-independent (likely convective/contact resistance) plus a small, weakly conductivity-dependent term.
- R3-mass (≤100 kg/m²) and R4-thickness (≤40mm) are the actual binding limits, and are generously satisfied by all light single-layer designs.
- Multi-layer copper cladding (e.g., 2mm Cu + 10mm Al) never beats pure graphite on mass, since copper's high density (8960) outweighs its conductivity benefit for this purpose — the flatness of R2 with material choice means the extra copper mass buys negligible thermal improvement.
- The lightest all-pass prior design is **10mm graphite at 18 kg/m²** (margin 3) — this is the record to beat.

Since R2 shows no measurable sensitivity to thickness from 10–30mm, and R1 is nowhere near binding, the primary lever for mass reduction is reducing graphite/aluminium thickness below the tested 10mm floor — but this is genuine extrapolation with no data point below 10mm, so I'm hedging with a graduated-risk portfolio rather than one extreme bet.

# No-iterative-feedback designer arm (arm C)

3 candidate(s) submitted in one call; none evaluated in this session.

| candidate | design | rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| c-0000 | 6 mm graphite | Single-layer graphite, thinned from the prior record's 10mm to 6mm. Areal mass = 0.006 m * 1800 kg/m3 = 10.8 kg/m2, well under the R3 100 kg/m2 cap and a 40% mass cut versus the lightest prior all-pass design (10mm graphite at 18 kg/m2). Thickness 6mm << R4's 40mm cap. Using the prior's implied screening relation T_screen = 399 + 60*(t/k), 6mm graphite gives T_screen = 399 + 60*(6/150) = 401.4K, comfortably under the 420K R1 cap (and the prior data shows R1 rises, not falls, with thickness, so thinning only helps this margin). For R2-hotspot, the prior constellation shows graphite's FE hotspot is essentially flat at 325K across 10/20/30mm thickness -- i.e., spreading resistance is already saturated well below 10mm, so the plate's own thickness contributes negligibly to the hotspot once above some modest floor. Reducing to 6mm is a moderate (40%) extrapolation below the tested floor, not an extreme one, so I expect the hotspot to remain close to 325K and thus comfortably clear the 340K limit with a plausible ~10-15K of margin. This is my primary bet for the lightest design I believe still meets every requirement. |
| c-0001 | 9 mm graphite | Single-layer graphite at 9mm, only a 10% reduction from the prior's directly-tested 10mm graphite point (18 kg/m2, all PASS, worst margin 3). Areal mass = 0.009*1800 = 16.2 kg/m2, a modest but low-risk improvement over the prior record. Thickness 9mm is far under the 40mm R4 cap. Screening: T_screen = 399 + 60*(9/150) = 402.6K, safely under 420K (and below the directly-tested 10mm graphite value of 403K, consistent with the observed trend that R1 rises with added thickness). Because this thickness is minimally extrapolated from a directly-scored, all-PASS prior point (10mm graphite, hotspot 325K, worst margin 3), I have high confidence the FE hotspot stays essentially at ~325K, deep inside the 340K R2 limit. This candidate serves as the conservative, near-certain-pass member of the set, trading a smaller mass saving for much lower extrapolation risk than the 6mm option. |
| c-0002 | 5 mm aluminium | Single-layer aluminium at 5mm, offering a differently-grounded bet: aluminium's higher conductivity (200 vs graphite's 150 W/mK) should give it more headroom against any thickness-driven rise in spreading resistance below the tested 10mm floor, even though its density (2700) is higher than graphite's (1800). Areal mass = 0.005*2700 = 13.5 kg/m2, still a 25% cut versus the prior record (10mm graphite, 18 kg/m2) and well under the 100 kg/m2 cap; thickness is far under the 40mm cap. Screening: T_screen = 399 + 60*(5/200) = 400.5K, comfortably under 420K. The prior constellation shows aluminium's FE hotspot flat at 324K across 10/20/30mm, only 16K below the 340K limit, and its higher conductivity should better resist any uptick from going thinner than any tested point. This candidate diversifies the portfolio's underlying assumption -- betting on conductivity margin rather than pure mass minimization -- as a hedge in case graphite's lower conductivity makes it more sensitive to the untested sub-10mm regime than aluminium. |

The harness evaluates this set through Avila Core after this session ends.

content.text:
## Final Report

I submitted 3 single-layer candidates for CASE-003, all as thin, single-material plates chosen to beat the prior record's lightest all-pass design (10mm graphite, 18 kg/m²):

| Candidate | Design | Areal mass | vs. prior record (18 kg/m²) |
|---|---|---|---|
| c-0000 | 6mm graphite | 10.8 kg/m² | −40% |
| c-0001 | 9mm graphite | 16.2 kg/m² | −10% |
| c-0002 | 5mm aluminium | 13.5 kg/m² | −25% |

**Reasoning:** The prior data revealed two things I leaned on heavily:
1. R1-screen fits a clean formula, T ≈ 399 + 60·(t/k), and gets *safer* as thickness decreases — never a binding concern for thin plates.
2. R2-hotspot (the real, ≤340K constraint) was essentially **flat with thickness** for each material (graphite held at 325K across 10/20/30mm; aluminium at 324K), suggesting spreading resistance was already saturated at 10mm and thickness itself contributes little to the hotspot once above some threshold.

Since R3 (mass) and R4 (thickness) were never close to binding for any light single-layer option, and multi-layer copper cladding never beat pure graphite/aluminium on mass (copper's density penalty outweighs its conductivity benefit here), the only real lever was pushing thickness below the tested 10mm floor — genuine extrapolation with no data point to confirm it.

I hedged that risk with a three-point graduated portfolio rather than one extreme bet: **c-0000 (6mm graphite)** is my most aggressive, lightest candidate and the one I believe is lightest while still meeting every requirement; **c-0001 (9mm graphite)** is a near-certain-pass fallback barely extrapolated from the directly-tested 10mm point; and **c-0002 (5mm aluminium)** diversifies the underlying assumption, betting on conductivity headroom rather than pure mass minimization in case graphite's lower conductivity makes it more sensitive to the untested thin-gauge regime.

No feedback was available at any point — this was the single, final submission per the arm-C protocol.
